plan: With a private value of $18, I want to win without overpaying. Since values are uniformly drawn between $0-$20, the expected opponent value is $10. Rational opponents will bid strategically near their value. I'll bid $15, which is slightly below my true value. This gives me room to potentially win without paying too close to my full value. If opponents bid aggressively, I'm protected; if they bid conservatively, I'm likely to win.

In a second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$20, the optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. Since my value is $16, I want to bid high enough to win, but not so high that I reduce my potential profit. Given the random distribution, other bidders might bid around their own values. I'll bid $15.90 - slightly under my true value to protect against overpaying, but still very likely to win if others bid rationally near their values.

In a single-round auction with values drawn from $0-$20, the optimal strategy is a "truth-telling" approach near my private value. Since my value is $14, I want to bid strategically to maximize profit. I'll bid slightly below my value to reduce risk of overpaying. Rational opponents will likely bid similarly relative to their own private values. A bid around $12-$13 balances winning probability with profit protection.
